Berkeley Springs.wildlife_intro:
Our crew's Berkeley Springs calls follow the ground the town sits on: warm Spring Ridge and the springs at the town's center, Cacapon Mountain rising west, wooded residential streets climbing the ridges around the historic core. That setting puts raccoons, gray squirrels, bats, striped skunks in regular contact with homes here, and most jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find. Every operator we send is a WVDNR-licensed Wildlife Damage Control Agent (WDCA), and we handle disposition the West Virginia way — exclusion and on-site liberation where the rules allow it, never a relocation promise.

In fall and winter, squirrels and rodents push into warm attics across the county, and spring brings denning raccoons looking for chimneys and soffits to raise young. Berkeley Springs layers historic spa-era homes and cottages in the valley with cabins and newer homes on the surrounding ridges. Call us at (844) 544-3498 when you first hear scratching or find droppings or digging — early jobs are almost always simpler jobs.

faqs.q: What should I do about a snake near my Paw Paw stone wall or woodpile?
faqs.a: Keep distance and call us. Rat snakes and the occasional copperhead hunt mice around stone walls and woodpiles here, and it is illegal to kill any snake in the wild in West Virginia. A licensed WDCA captures problem snakes non-lethally and liberates them at the site of capture.
